summary: @kropa/baileys ships obfuscated license-guard with char-code-hidden exfiltration endpoint
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library that adds two concerning components not present in upstream. lib/Utils/license-guard.js is a heavily obfuscated module (hex-prefixed identifiers, string-array indirection) whose intent is intentionally hidden from reviewers. lib/Socket/messages-send.js at lines 425 and 436 reconstructs an outbound HTTPS URL from a String.fromCharCode numeric array; decoding the character codes yields the host https://fiora.nixel.my.id/. The destination is assembled via char-code obfuscation rather than appearing as a plain string, so it will not surface in trivial source review, and the host is unrelated to any WhatsApp/Baileys infrastructure. The call sits inside the message-send path, meaning normal use of the library's advertised API (sending WhatsApp messages) triggers traffic to this third-party endpoint controlled by the fork's author. The combination of obfuscated identifier-guard code plus a char-code-hidden non-first-party destination on the message pipeline is the fingerprint of covert data relay / credential or message interception layered on top of a legitimate library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
